findings.title: Results print Table 1 counts as cohort percentages
findings.description: Results and Discussion state that wound gapping, seroma, erythema and infection occurred in 12%, 10%, 18% and 20% of the whole cohort. findings.title: Table 2 BMI range 23.0-45.0 contradicts BMI>30 inclusion
findings.description: Inclusion required BMI>30 and Methods state there is no group with BMI below 30 because the study was restricted to obese women. findings.title: Registered 1-month primary outcome not the paper's 7-day follow-up
findings.description: NCT03354078 was first submitted 19 November 2017 after a stated 18 June 2017 start, so registration is retrospective. The registered primary outcome is participants without seroma, erythema, and infection at one month after cesarean. The paper says most complications were diagnosed at 7 days and does not report 1-month results. Registry eligibility is age 18-40 years; the paper includes ages 25-35. The paper dates the study to December 2017, while the registry lists completion 23 November 2017 and the journal received the manuscript 1 December 2017.

findings.title: Methods omit outcome definitions, analysis, randomization, and ethics
findings.description: This interventional RCT reports wound gapping, seroma, erythema, infection, and a 42-event composite without diagnostic criteria, a named statistical test for Table 4, a sample-size calculation, sequence generation, or allocation concealment. Skin closure is never specified even though surgeons closed skin and subcutaneous layers. The only ethics statement is informed consent; no ethics-committee approval is recorded.
findings.quote: Randomization of cases was done to the 400 pregnant women who were consented to participate in the study and were distributed in two groups: group A and group B. The randomization allocation was 1:1.

consequence.explanation: Unspecified skin closure and undefined wound outcomes block reproduction of the primary comparisons.

findings.notes: Ten surgeons received randomly distributed patients; analysis treats 397 women as independent. Table 6 enters eight covariates against 42 composite events. Innocent reading: details exist in an uncited local protocol.

anchors.label: Methods, randomization
anchors.quote: Randomization of cases was done to the 400 pregnant women who were consented to participate in the study and were distributed in two groups: group A and group B. The randomization allocation was 1:1.

anchors.label: Consent section
anchors.quote: All pregnant women who accepted to participate in this study signed an informed consent after complete explanation of the procedure to the participant woman.

anchors.label: Methods, surgeons and skin closure
anchors.quote: Ten surgeons performed the whole procedure of CS including the closure of subcutaneous and skin layer, all these surgeons were the consultants and specialists

adjudication.rationale: Methods describe a prospective 1:1 randomized trial but never define diagnostic criteria for gapping, seroma, erythema, or infection, never name the Table 4 test or a sample-size calculation, and never describe sequence generation, allocation concealment, or skin-closure technique. Informed consent is recorded; no ethics-committee approval appears. These gaps block reproduction of the primary comparison.
adjudication.title_was: Methods omit outcome definitions, analysis, randomization, and ethics
adjudication.description_was: This interventional RCT reports wound gapping, seroma, erythema, infection, and a 42-event composite without diagnostic criteria, a named statistical test, a sample-size calculation, sequence generation, or allocation concealment. Skin closure method is never specified even though surgeons closed skin and subcutaneous layers and the primary claims are wound complications. The only ethics statement is that participants signed informed consent; no committee, protocol number, or Helsinki statement is given. Selective suction drainage for oozing is allowed but not reported by arm.

findings.title: Citation [1] does not support the 3% to 30% CS complication range
findings.description: The paper cites Brown et al. 2010 for cesarean wound-complication incidence ranging from 3% to 30%. That paper is a plastic-surgery study of psychosocial distress and self-rated scar severity in 82 patients and does not report cesarean wound-complication incidence. Wound-infection risk factors are cited to Menacker and Hamilton 2010 (ref 7) plus Wloch et al. 2012 (ref 8); the Menacker NCHS data brief is about US cesarean-rate trends, not wound-infection predictors, while Wloch is an SSI risk-factor cohort.
findings.quote: Postoperative wound complications are one of the great issues in CS with an incidence ranging from 3% to 30% [1].

consequence.explanation: The 3-30% incidence figure is not supported by the cited source; the trial's own estimates do not use this range.

findings.notes: The 3-30% band is widely quoted in cesarean SSI papers; the defect is the citation, not necessarily the number. Ref 8 (Wloch) does support SSI risk factors.

anchors.label: Introduction, incidence claim
anchors.quote: Postoperative wound complications are one of the great issues in CS with an incidence ranging from 3% to 30% [1].

anchors.label: Introduction, risk-factor claim
anchors.quote: Obesity, operative time, diabetes, age of the patient, anemia, associated infection (e.g. chorioamnionitis), delayed labor with many vaginal examinations, and reduced nutrition are recognized risk factors for wound infections [7,8].

anchors.label: Reference [1]
anchors.quote: Brown BC, Moss TP, McGrouther DA, et al. Skin scar preconceptions must be challenged: importance of selfperception in skin scarring. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg.2010;63(6):1022–1029.

anchors.label: Reference [7]
anchors.quote: Menacker F, Hamilton BE. Recent trends in cesarean delivery in the United States. NCHS data brief, no 35. Hyattsville, MD: National Center for Health Statistics; 2010.

adjudication.rationale: Reference [1] as printed is Brown et al. 2010 on skin-scar self-perception, which cannot support the Introduction's 3% to 30% cesarean wound-complication incidence. Reference [7] is an NCHS brief on cesarean-delivery trends, cited for wound-infection risk factors; [8] (Wloch et al.) is on-point. These are background citations, not results.

adjudication.summary: The most trust-undermining defect is Table 2's BMI range of 23.0–45.0 against the Methods inclusion rule BMI>30 and the explicit claim that the study has no women with BMI below 30; the title and abstract present the trial as a study of obese women. Results and Discussion also print Table 1 event counts (12, 10, 18, 20 of 397) as cohort percentages, inflating gapping, seroma, erythema, and infection about four-fold relative to the table's 3%, 2.5%, 4.5%, and 5%. Figure 1 and the Methods attrition narrative reconcile (411 assessed, 11 declined, 400 randomized 1:1, 3 lost, 199 and 198 analysed), and the six result tables' cell counts, percentages, and Table 4 odds ratios match one another. Methods never define the four wound outcomes, name the Table 4 test, report a sample-size calculation, describe sequence generation or allocation concealment, specify skin closure, or record ethics-committee approval. A corrigendum should correct the BMI range or the inclusion claim, restore the prose incidences to the table values, and supply the missing CONSORT items. This review did not independently re-fetch the ClinicalTrials.gov record, did not establish intent, and the table-level arithmetic screen otherwise reconciled on the printed values.

rounding_convention.note: Values that fail the round-half convention but are consistent if the reporter TRUNCATES (SPSS's default, and several journal styles). NOT a finding and never counted as one: a single instance is a house style. The RATE is the signal -- this class of anomaly is commoner in papers with more serious problems, so a high proportion is grounds to look harder, not evidence in itself.

grace.reading: Nothing needed an allowance; every item reconciled on its printed values.

sd_convention.note: Values that fail under the sample (Bessel, n-1) SD but are consistent under the POPULATION (n) SD -- numpy's std default and Excel's STDEVP. NOT a finding and never counted as one: choosing a convention is not fabrication. The RATE is the signal, on the same reasoning as the rounding convention above.

harness_sweep.why: These checks were aimed by the harness, not by the model: every eligible target in the paper's tables was enumerated and checked. That makes their coverage identical from run to run, which the model-aimed checks are not -- two runs of this pipeline on one paper overlapped on 0 of 10 model-aimed targets.
